PullRequest.Title: Add prioritized Sessions Inbox notifications view
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
- add a new `inboxOne` Sessions contribution with a dedicated **Inbox** custom view for prioritized, actionable notifications, behind a hidden and advanced setting
- introduce `IInboxNotificationsService` to aggregate notifications from session lifecycle state (`NeedsInput`, unread `Completed` sessions)
- add session-linked PR notifications using existing client-side GitHub models:
  - failing required CI checks
  - passing required CI checks (merge-ready signal)
  - unresolved Copilot review comments
  - **merged pull requests** (session cleanup signal)
- for the CI / review / merge PR notifications, add one-click actions that submit the matching agent skill to the session's chat **in the background** — the same universal mechanism as the in-session **Fix Checks / Address Comments** — so they work for **cloud and agent-host sessions alike** and never open or navigate to the session:
  - **Fix CI Failures** → `/fix-ci`
  - **Address Reviews** → `/act-on-feedback`
  - **Merge Pull Request** → `/merge`
  - failing CI **and** unresolved Copilot comments on the same session are addressed together in one turn (`/fix-ci and /act-on-feedback`)
- show an inline progress spinner on the action while the request is submitting, and surface an error notification if the submission fails
- for merged pull request notifications, add direct actions to:
  - **Archive Session**
  - **Delete Session**
  - optional **Always {Action}** dropdown behavior wired to existing merged-session lifecycle settings
- keep a provider-neutral external publish seam (`publishExternalNotification`) for additional integrations
- integrate an **Inbox** shortcut section in the Sessions list that opens the custom view directly
- add accessibility support for the Inbox surface (focus context key, accessible help + view providers, and `accessibility.verbosity.inboxNotifications`)
- gate the whole feature behind an experimental setting `chat.agentSessions.inbox.enabled` (off by default, `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`), mirrored into a `ChatInboxEnabledContext` context key; the Inbox section, view, and Show Inbox command are hidden unless the setting (or an experiment) enables it
- add focused unit tests for notification derivation/persistence, PR/CI/comment/merged signal derivation, and accessible-content output

## Intentional Scope
This change does not add new agent-host async event contracts. PR/CI/comment signals are derived from existing client-side session-linked GitHub models for MVP, and can later switch to unified async triggers with minimal churn. The CI / review / merge actions reuse the existing in-session skill-submission path (`IChatService.acquireOrLoadSession` + `sendRequest` with `agentIdSilent`), so they run identically on cloud and agent-host sessions without opening the session.

## Enablement
The Inbox is experimental and off by default. It is gated by the machine-scoped setting `chat.agentSessions.inbox.enabled` (tags: `experimental`, `advanced`; `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`), mirrored into the `ChatInboxEnabledContext` context key. When disabled, the Inbox shortcut section in the Sessions list, the Inbox custom view (restore + auto-hide), and the **Show Inbox** command/keybinding are all hidden. Toggling the setting updates the Sessions list reactively without a reload. This mirrors the Automations enablement pattern (`chat.automations.enabled`).

## Testing
- `npx eslint src/vs/sessions/contrib/inboxOne/browser/inboxNotificationsView.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/inboxOne/browser/inboxNotificationsService.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/inboxOne/test/browser/inboxNotificationsService.test.ts`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/inboxOne/test/browser/inboxNotificationsService.test.ts`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/inboxOne/test/browser/inboxNotificationsAccessibility.test.ts`

## Inbox Event → Actions (Now/Next/Later Order)

| Priority Tier | Event | Actions Offered |
|---|---|---|
| Now | Needs input | Open Session · Done |
| Now | Failing CI on linked PR | Open Session · Fix CI Failures · Done |
| Now | Unresolved Copilot review comments | Open Session · Address Reviews · Done |
| Next | Passing CI on linked PR | Open Session · Merge Pull Request · Done |
| Next | Pull request merged | Open Session · Archive Session · Delete Session · Done |
| Later | Completed session (unread) | Open Session · Mark as Read · Done |

The CI / review / merge actions submit their agent skill to the session in the background — `Fix CI Failures` → `/fix-ci`, `Address Reviews` → `/act-on-feedback`, `Merge Pull Request` → `/merge` (and `/fix-ci and /act-on-feedback` when the session has both failing CI and unresolved Copilot comments). A spinner shows on the button while the request submits; an error notification is shown if it fails.

## Inbox PR Action Mechanism (Cloud vs Agent-Host)

All three CI / review / merge actions run through one code path — `IChatService.acquireOrLoadSession(session.resource)` then `sendRequest(session.resource, query, { agentIdSilent: session.resource.scheme })` — so the Inbox behaves the same regardless of provider and never navigates to the session.

| Session kind | Routing key (`agentIdSilent` = `resource.scheme`) | Where the skill runs |
|---|---|---|
| Agent-host (local / remote) | `agent-host-*` | Local/remote agent-host process runs the skill against the PR |
| Cloud Copilot | `copilot-cloud-agent` | Cloud coding-agent task runs the skill server-side |

## Agent Merge "Always" Opt-In Prompt Behavior

The immediate action always submits the agent skill (above). Separately, the Inbox tracks usage of these actions globally (profile-scoped, per action) and offers a milestone-based opt-in to enable the corresponding **Agent Merge** default. Because those defaults only take effect for **agent-host** sessions, the **Always {Action}** dropdown (and its opt-in prompt) is shown only on agent-host session notifications and is hidden on cloud sessions.

| Tracked event in Inbox | Action being tracked | "Always" dropdown action | Prompt cadence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Failing CI on linked PR | Fix CI Failures | Always Fix CI Failures | On 10th use, then every +10 (20, 30, …) |
| Unresolved Copilot review comments | Address Reviews | Always Address Reviews | On 10th use, then every +10 (20, 30, …) |
| Passing CI on linked PR | Merge Pull Request | Always Merge Pull Request | On 10th use, then every +10 (20, 30, …) |

Prompt details:
- shown only for agent-host sessions, and only when that action is not already globally enabled
- primary action: **Always {Action}**
- secondary action: **Not Now**
- checkbox: **Don't ask again for this action** (suppresses future prompts for that action)
- opting in writes global Agent Merge defaults, so the auto-behavior applies to future agent-host sessions

## Merged PR "Always" Cleanup Behavior

For merged PR notifications, selecting **Always Archive Session** or **Always Delete Session** writes existing lifecycle settings (`ConfigurationTarget.USER`) to enable automatic merged-session cleanup:

- `chat.agentSessions.autoMarkAsDoneMergedSessionsAfterDays = 15`
- `chat.agentSessions.autoDeleteMarkedAsDoneMergedSessionsAfterDays = 15` (for Always Delete)

## Inbox Telemetry (Privacy-Constrained)

This PR adds inbox-surface telemetry specific to actions taken in the Inbox view (`agents/inboxInteraction`) and keeps payloads bounded to interaction metadata.

### Logged interaction coverage
- toolbar interactions (sort mode changes, completed visibility toggle)
- section interactions (expand/collapse)
- list/update interactions (deferred update banner actions)
- card-level actions and dropdown actions
- inline needs-input submissions (confirmation, tool confirmation, question carousel)
- detail-pane interactions (open full session, open PR/evidence links)
- selection lifecycle and dwell timing (select/deselect)

### Logged metadata
- interaction name and trigger surface
- outcome (`attempt`, `success`, `failure`, `skipped`)
- duration (for async actions and dwell)
- bounded notification/action kinds
- whether a session is associated
- command id for command-backed actions
- per-view trajectory fields (`viewInstanceId`, monotonic `sequence`)

### Explicitly not logged
- session titles
- AI-generated summaries, responses, or request/response snippet text
- typed inline-answer text
- command arguments or tool payload content
- hashed per-notification identifiers
- inline answer-shape/length/count metadata

## Follow-up (not included in this PR)
- add an explicit **"Inbox was useful"** feedback affordance to collect direct user sentiment on Inbox usefulness.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call path, 60-second schedules, model-key coalescing, and underlying network request count are all explicit in repository code and corroborated by the new polling-count test. Exact user PR counts vary, affecting severity magnitude but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub REST/GraphQL requests and API quota
Findings.PerformanceScaling: After model sharing coalesces duplicate session references, cost still grows with the number of distinct PRs linked from all non-archived sessions: each open PR keeps three 60-second pollers, whose refresh paths issue at least five API requests per cycle (PR metadata, reviews, PR metadata again for review threads, review threads, and CI checks), plus pagination.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Continuous excessive network traffic and GitHub API throttling that can degrade all GitHub-backed UI in the window.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, merely enabling the experimental Inbox did not create any all-session GitHub pollers; existing GitHub models were polled only by their existing active consumers.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new enabled-service autorun walks every session and `ensureGitHubModels` starts PR, review-thread, and CI polling for each linked open PR, regardless of whether the Inbox view is open or the session is recent/actionable.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 1741 calls `pullRequestModelRef.object.startPolling()` from the new all-session derivation; added RIGHT lines 1761 and 1781 do the same for review-thread and CI models.
Findings.Title: Stop polling every historical pull request each minute
Findings.Impact: With tens of historical session-linked PRs, an enabled but unopened Inbox can generate hundreds of GitHub requests per minute (for example, 50 distinct open PRs imply at least 250 requests/minute), consuming bandwidth/battery and exhausting rate limits.
Findings.Evidence: `ensureGitHubModels` is called for every session at lines 754-756. This line starts the PR poller, with additional review-thread and CI pollers at lines 1761 and 1781. All three model implementations use a 60,000 ms default interval. Their fetchers show the PR refresh performs two requests, review-thread refresh performs two, and CI refresh performs one. Reference collections share models by PR key, so this count is per distinct PR rather than per duplicate session; the added test at `inboxNotificationsService.test.ts:891` explicitly expects three live pollers for one open draft PR.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not attach 60-second pollers to every historical PR. Bound the tracked set (for example to active/recent actionable sessions), use a slower/coalesced background refresh for the badge, and only enable the fast PR/review/CI polling while the Inbox is visible; dispose those subscriptions when hidden.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The eager all-session loop, cold/warm guard, local and remote load boundaries, unbounded launch pattern, and retained references are explicit. The number and size of unread histories vary by profile, so magnitude is reflected in medium severity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Persisted-session reads or remote session requests, parsed transcript objects, and retained chat models
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cold cost grows with every unique unread completed session (and every chat of each needs-input session); distinct resources are launched concurrently, while only already-loaded duplicate resources are coalesced.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: A burst of background I/O/network and history replay plus retained-memory/CPU pressure immediately after enablement or restore, competing with interactive startup work.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, enabling the Sessions surface did not load every unread completed session's chat model merely to populate a hidden Inbox; histories were loaded by existing consumers when needed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: As soon as the feature is enabled, the new autorun traverses all non-archived sessions and this line eagerly calls `ensureChatModelLoaded` for every unread completed session, even if the Inbox is never opened. The resulting model reference is retained until the session leaves that state.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 801 invokes `ensureChatModelLoaded` for every unread completed session from the feature-enable autorun; added RIGHT line 2384 launches the underlying asynchronous load.
Findings.Title: Load completed chat histories only when their cards are viewed
Findings.Impact: Profiles with many unread completed cloud or local sessions pay to fetch/read and replay all full histories during restore, although only a viewport-sized subset of cards can be inspected; this can increase startup contention and memory use.
Findings.Evidence: Lines 789-803 iterate the complete session collection and select all unread completed sessions. `ensureChatModelLoaded` at lines 2368-2398 starts `acquireOrLoadSession` without a shared limiter and retains each reference. The transitive implementation reads local persisted session data (`chatServiceImpl.ts:760-780`) or calls the remote provider's `getOrCreateChatSession` and replays its full history (`chatServiceImpl.ts:951-1005`). The PR's own enablement test records a chat load immediately when the setting is turned on, without opening the view.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep completed notifications derived from session metadata initially, and acquire the completed chat only from `requestPreview`/selection when that card becomes visible. If some proactive loading is required, cap it to a small recent set behind a shared limiter and release offscreen/inactive models.

Scenarios.Scenario: Window restore or setting enablement while the Inbox view remains closed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The service is instantiated from the Sessions list and its enabled autoruns start immediately. GitHub refreshes are required before PR/CI/review notifications and their badge state become authoritative; chat loads are required for inline pending parts and completed-response content. The calls are not awaited by window restore, so they are off the direct startup critical path but compete with startup CPU, I/O, network, and memory.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh and poll PR metadata/reviews, review threads, and CI checks through GitHub REST/GraphQL APIs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per distinct linked PR after reference-key sharing: one PR model, and for each open PR one review-thread model plus one CI model. Their refresh paths issue at least five requests per open PR per 60-second cycle, plus pagination.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No all-session Inbox consumer or recurring pollers existed before this diff; GitHub polling came from existing active feature consumers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for fresh PR-derived Inbox state; otherwise background traffic continues while the Inbox is closed and can throttle other GitHub work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire or restore chat sessions, reading persisted local sessions or resolving remote sessions and replaying full history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One unique main chat per unread completed session, plus every chat of every needs-input session; warm already-loaded chats are skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These histories were loaded by existing consumers on demand, not en masse when an experimental Inbox setting became enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by restore, but required for rich notification content and competes with startup; remote/local histories remain retained through model references.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All non-archived sessions. After model sharing, GitHub work scales with distinct linked PRs; chat work scales with unique chats of needs-input sessions plus one main chat for every unread completed session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: GitHub initial refreshes and independent model pollers are started for every distinct key without an Inbox-level limiter; each model coalesces concurrent refreshes for its own key only and polls every 60 seconds. Chat loads are launched with `void` for all distinct resources; ChatService coalesces only duplicate resource loads, while distinct local/remote loads can be active together.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GitHub reference collections share models by PR (and CI head SHA), and a WeakSet prevents duplicate initial refresh of the same live model, but polling repeats indefinitely and failures do not reduce cadence. ChatService warm models avoid the boundary, and the service's loading/reference maps coalesce duplicate chat resources; cold histories are all loaded and retained while their sessions remain relevant.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the all-session loops, per-key coalescing, 60-second poll intervals, underlying API methods, cold chat boundaries, and retained references are explicit and corroborated by added tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of historical linked PRs and unread completed sessions varies by profile, as does history size and API latency. Tens of sessions/PRs are realistic for the target background-agent workflow; this uncertainty changes severity, not the established all-collection mechanisms.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: one high-severity recurring GitHub boundary fan-out and one medium-severity eager chat-history load were submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening and scrolling the Inbox, then selecting a notification
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial cards render synchronously. One-line preview generation begins only after a card intersects the viewport and is off the first DOM render critical path; selected completed/needs-input detail generation is on the detail-pane content path but has a fallback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send utility-model chat requests for visible card previews and selected-item detail/classification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one preview per uncached visible signature; one detail request and one classification request per selected uncached item, all behind concurrency 3.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Inbox and these model calls did not exist before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Preview work is deferred from initial rendering; detail work affects only the selected detail pane and can fall back to existing text.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Active notifications in enabled categories determine DOM cardinality; intersecting cards determine preview requests. A selected item determines one detail summary and one subsequent classification.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Preview, detail, and classification model work shares a Limiter capped at 3. IntersectionObserver gates previews, and signature/in-flight sets coalesce repeats. DOM cards are rebuilt serially for the active collection.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Preview signatures have in-flight deduplication and a 200-entry LRU; detail summaries use in-flight deduplication and a 50-entry LRU. Fallbacks are invalidated when language models appear. Offscreen cards do not request previews.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the lazy boundaries and limiter; medium for potential DOM scale because realistic notification counts are not established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large active-notification collections would make the non-virtualized DOM rebuild more expensive, but the diff provides no evidence of a realistic cardinality or measured jank sufficient for another finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: expensive model work is lazy, deduplicated, cached, and concurrency-bounded; full-list DOM rebuilding alone lacks enough impact evidence.

Scenarios.Scenario: Running an Inbox PR action or answering inline input
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The clicked action waits for one session acquisition and one send/notification operation; this is the user-requested action's critical path. Inline answers mutate the already-loaded chat model and may update session read state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire a cold remote chat session and send a slash-command request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One acquire/load and one send per click; failing CI and review feedback for the same session are combined into a single send.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Inbox action path is new, while the underlying in-session submission mechanism already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly determines completion latency for the requested action, but does not fan out over notifications.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist usage counters, dismissal IDs, or lifecycle configuration for the explicit action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A bounded number of storage writes per click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These Inbox-specific writes did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small user-paced writes; no established performance regression.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected notification per user action; combined CI/review work is intentionally coalesced into one slash-command turn for the session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: User-paced. Each click starts one action; the corresponding button is disabled while agent-merge submission runs. ChatService coalesces an in-progress load for the same resource.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Already-loaded chat sessions avoid restore; cold session acquisition uses ChatService's per-resource load coalescing. There is no collection-wide loop on this action path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency varies, but operation count is fixed per user action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: boundary work is user-initiated, fixed-cardinality, and same-resource loads are coalesced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full 35-file diff. Submitted two introduced regressions: recurring all-session GitHub polling fan-out and eager loading/retention of unread completed chat histories. Viewport model generation and action paths were checked and are bounded by laziness, caching, coalescing, or user pacing.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
